# Native table-corner references

The reference application exported the original OPC/XML controls on 2026-09-18.
`tools/canvas_border_corner_fixture.py` creates `border-corner-controls.docx`;
`--mixed-counts` changes the final control's left border from double to triple;
`--colors` assigns a different color to each side.
The scaffold is the independently authored compound-border fixture. No corpus
content or third-party document-engine output is used to create the controls.

Both documents include paragraph and table cases: equal double, equal triple,
unequal double widths, and mixed continuous patterns. `native.pdf` and
`mixed-counts-native.pdf` retain the reference application exports. Additional compound and frame
references are retained in `../compound-borders`.

The reference application connects matching style/size borders by joining outer ink bands to outer
bands and inner bands to inner bands. With different styles or sizes, the reference application's
horizontal bands span the corner and its vertical bands stop at their inside
edge. The mixed-count control also demonstrates this with two versus three
strokes. These are observations of painting details not numerically specified
by ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.4.38, 17.4.66 and 17.18.2.

`reference.json` records source/PDF SHA-256 values and each table's filled
PDF rectangles and colors in drawing order, normalized to the minimum painted x/y. Rectangles
were extracted from PDF path objects and grouped between table-label baselines.
The browser tests compare corner ink occupancy with these independent shapes
for all 36 tables, excluding points within 0.3pt of either renderer's rectangle
edges to allow the reference application's 600dpi width rounding and PDF placement precision. They
also exercise text editing, export/reopen and exact OPC undo. Unit tests cover
all corner directions, frame direction, cell clipping, row-height prepasses,
borderless tables and exclusion of multi-edge junctions.

The isolated `border-frame-only-{top,left,bottom,right}.docx` controls, generated by
`tools/canvas_border_frame_flags_fixture.py`, add a reference-specific distinction:
the left table edge's frame flag reverses its straight body but not its corner
caps. It does not reverse the left paragraph border. The vertical flag controls
the straight body; the top/bottom flag controls the corresponding right corner
cap. Each isolated flag rules out accidental propagation from the other sides.
The retained `frame-only-*-native.pdf` exports prove the behavior independently
of the source template. The initial compound-border implementation missed the
left-body and right-cap distinctions; these references and color/occupancy
checks correct them. The colored controls show that horizontal ink owns a
matching corner's overlap; vertical ink stops at that band's edge.

Open differences: T/cross junctions and dashed-pattern corners retain their
existing behavior. Paragraph double/triple width and frame placement differ
from the reference application in these controls and require separate layout corrections. This
reference set does not certify full-document pixel equivalence.
